title: Who needs an RSA competency card in NSW, and how often must it be renewed?
description: Who must hold an NSW RSA competency card, the 90 day interim certificate, the 5 year refresher, licensee duties and the on the spot fines that apply.
shortAnswer: In New South Wales, anyone who sells, serves or supplies alcohol, and security staff and crowd controllers monitoring patrons, must complete Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA) training with a Liquor & Gaming NSW approved provider. Completion gives a 90 day interim certificate, then an NSW competency card valid for five years. Holders renew by completing an online refresher before the card expires, and licensees can be fined for letting unendorsed staff work.
keyTakeaways: The NSW RSA course includes the national unit Provide responsible service of alcohol (SITHFAB021) plus NSW specific content, and must be delivered by a Liquor & Gaming NSW approved training provider.
An interim certificate lets a new worker start immediately and is valid for 90 days, during which the worker completes an identity check at Service NSW to get the photo competency card.
The competency card is valid for five years; every endorsement on one card expires five years from the earliest endorsement, and a 60 to 90 minute online refresher renews it.
Under the Liquor Regulation 2018, a worker without a current RSA endorsement faces a $220 penalty notice ($440 in a prescribed precinct), and a licensee who permits it faces $1,100.
The card must be carried, physically or digitally, whenever the worker is in a role that requires it.
jurisdiction: Australia (New South Wales): Liquor Act 2007 and Liquor Regulation 2018
regulator: Liquor & Gaming NSW (part of the NSW Government Department of Creative Industries, Tourism, Hospitality and Sport)
appliesTo: Bar staff, food and beverage attendants and anyone else who sells, serves or supplies alcohol on licensed premises
Retail liquor salespersons, winery and brewery staff, and promotional staff
Security staff, crowd controllers and RSA marshals monitoring patron behavior
Licensees, approved managers and club secretaries

sections.heading: Who needs RSA training in NSW?

blocks.text: Anyone who will sell, serve or supply alcohol in New South Wales needs RSA training, and so does a security staff member or crowd controller whose job is monitoring customer behavior. [Liquor & Gaming NSW](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/get-started) treats RSA as the entry credential for almost every customer facing role in a licensed venue.

The regulator's [RSA page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/rsa) lists the roles covered: service staff, food and beverage attendants, retail liquor salespersons, winery and brewery staff, promotional staff, RSA marshals, security staff and crowd controllers, and volunteers. Volunteers are included on the same footing as paid staff, which matters for clubs, community events and festivals that rely on unpaid helpers.

Licensees also need RSA. Licensees must hold the appropriate RSA training before they complete Licensee Training, and most new licensees, approved managers and club secretaries must complete [Licensee Training or Advanced Licensee Training](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/lt-alt), generally within 60 days of provisional approval or of lodging the application.

sections.heading: What does the NSW RSA course cover?

blocks.text: The NSW RSA course combines the national unit of competency Provide responsible service of alcohol (SITHFAB021) with content specific to New South Wales. The NSW layer covers state liquor laws, managing intoxication, preventing underage drinking and harm minimization.

Only Liquor & Gaming NSW approved training providers can deliver the course. A Statement of Attainment for SITHFAB021 from another state does not on its own make someone eligible to work in NSW; the NSW competency card is the credential an inspector will ask for. Employers recruiting interstate staff should plan for the NSW course rather than assume portability.

sections.heading: How do the interim certificate and competency card work?

blocks.text: On passing the course, the worker receives an interim certificate that is valid for 90 days and allows them to work immediately. Within that window the worker takes the interim certificate and identity documents to Service NSW, has a photo taken, and receives the NSW competency card.

items: Complete the course with an approved provider and receive the interim certificate (valid 90 days).
Visit Service NSW with the interim certificate and identity documents for a photo and identity check.
Receive the digital card shortly after the photo is taken, and the physical card in the mail, which the regulator says takes 2 to 4 weeks.
Carry the physical or digital card whenever working in a role that requires it.

blocks.text: The [competency card guidance](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/competency-cards) says the card is valid for five years. One card can carry several endorsements, such as RSA and Responsible Conduct of Gambling (RCG); if a person holds more than one, they all expire five years from the earliest endorsement received. That rule can shorten an endorsement gained later, so expiry dates should be taken from the card, not calculated from the most recent course.

sections.heading: How often must the RSA be refreshed in NSW?

blocks.text: RSA must be refreshed every five years. A worker whose training was completed within the last five years completes the RSA Refresher, an online course the regulator says takes 60 to 90 minutes; a worker whose training was more than five years ago must complete the full course again.

The refresher should be completed before the card expires. Liquor & Gaming NSW allows a 28 day grace period after expiry, but only where the identity check was completed before the card expired. In practice, a business should schedule refreshers several weeks ahead of the expiry date shown on each card rather than relying on the grace period.

blocks.title: Primary text: Liquor & Gaming NSW
blocks.text: "If you hold more than one endorsement, they all expire 5 years from the earliest endorsement received."

sections.heading: What are the penalties for working without RSA in NSW?

blocks.text: Both the worker and the licensee can be fined. The regulator's [fines page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/competency-cards/fines) lists penalty notice amounts under the Liquor Regulation 2018 (LR2018), which are higher for staff in a prescribed precinct.

blocks.text: Workers can also be fined if they cannot present a valid card when an enforcement officer asks. Because the licensee's exposure is five times the worker's, the business has the stronger incentive to check cards before a first shift and to track expiry.

sections.heading: What should a licensee's RSA records show?

blocks.text: A licensee's records should show, for every rostered person in a covered role, a current endorsement on the day they worked. The table below maps each NSW obligation to the role, the frequency and the evidence an inspector or internal auditor would expect; it is an illustrative template, not a regulator form.

blocks.text: Recording the earliest endorsement date for each person, rather than the latest course date, prevents the most common tracking error. For the general method, see [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) and [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles). Venues that also handle food should read the separate [NSW food safety supervisor requirements](/regulations/nsw-food-safety-supervisor-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats the NSW competency card as an external credential with a defined expiry rule, and maps venue specific procedures, such as refusal of service and intoxication management, to assessable outcomes that sit alongside it. That lets a multi venue operator show which staff were assessed on which house policy version as well as holding a current card. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Can someone start serving alcohol in NSW before the photo card arrives?
faqs.a: Yes. The interim certificate issued on completing the course allows the person to work immediately and is valid for 90 days. Within that period they must complete the identity check at Service NSW. The digital card becomes available shortly after the photo is taken, and the physical card follows in the mail.

faqs.q: Is an interstate RSA certificate valid in NSW?
faqs.a: Liquor & Gaming NSW requires the course to be delivered by one of its approved training providers and issues the NSW competency card as the credential. A worker trained in another state should complete the NSW course with an approved provider before working in a role that requires RSA in New South Wales.

faqs.q: Do volunteers at a club or event need RSA in NSW?
faqs.a: Yes. Liquor & Gaming NSW lists volunteers among the people who must complete RSA training, alongside service staff, retail liquor salespersons, promotional staff and security. The same competency card and five year refresher rules apply to volunteers as to paid staff.

faqs.q: What happens if an NSW competency card has already expired?
faqs.a: If the identity check was completed before expiry, a 28 day grace period applies to complete the refresher. If the original RSA training was more than five years ago and the card has lapsed, the regulator says the full course must be completed again rather than the online refresher.
